title_en: Baird Strategas’ Todd Sohn on ETFs: What’s New and What’s Next
title_zh: Baird Strategas 的 Todd Sohn 谈 ETF：新动向与下一步
subtitle_zh: ProShares Hyman 拆解自动赎回型与备兑看涨 ETF，Todd Sohn 盘点年度 ETF 故事与空白。
description: Baird Strategas’ Todd Sohn on ETFs: What’s New and What’s Next

turns.en: The demand is coming from the need for income on the front end of Gen X. We don't have defined benefit plans and the boomers right before me don't have defined benefit plans.
turns.zh: 需求来自于收入的需要，来自 X 世代前端这一代人。我们没有固定收益（defined benefit）养老金计划，我前面那批婴儿潮一代也没有固定收益养老金计划。

turns.en: And if you do the math 60 40 portfolio, even with a generous five or six percent yield on your fixed income, that's two, two and a half percent.
turns.zh: 你要是算一笔账，60/40 的投资组合，就算你的固定收益部分给到 5% 到 6% 的慷慨收益率，那也就 2%、2.5%。

turns.en: That's not enough for people to to run their lives on. All right. Joining me will be Simeon Hyman, global investment strategist at pro shares who currently offers 163 ETFs, over $100 billion in assets.
turns.zh: 这不足以支撑人们的生活。好，接下来请到的嘉宾是 Simeon Hyman，ProShares 的全球投资策略师，ProShares 目前提供 163 只 ETF、逾 1000 亿美元资产。

turns.en: And back in August, they launched a suite of auto callable ETFs, which I will tell you, this is a category that continues to expand overall.
turns.zh: 今年八月他们推出了一整套自动赎回型（auto-callable）ETF，我得说，这是一个整体还在不断扩张的品类。

turns.en: The first auto callable ETF launched in June of last year, 2025, and already there are now over 30 auto callable ETFs with about $6 billion in assets.
turns.zh: 第一只自动赎回型 ETF 是去年，2025 年六月推出的，到现在已经有超过 30 只自动赎回型 ETF，大约 60 亿美元资产。

turns.en: And actually, I've seen a number of auto callable ETF filings with the SEC. So there's clearly a growing pipeline here. But bigger picture, auto callable ETFs fit into what I refer to as the alternative income category, where investors are seeking income solutions outside of traditional bond exposure, areas like cover call ETFs and other options based or derivative type strategies.
turns.zh: 其实我看到不少自动赎回型 ETF 向 SEC 递交的注册申请，所以这条管线显然在扩大。但更大层面看，自动赎回型 ETF 属于我所说的另类收益（alternative income）类别，投资者在寻找传统债券敞口之外的收益解决方案，比如备兑看涨（cover call）ETF 和其他期权类或衍生品型策略。

turns.en: And so Simeon Hyman are going to walk through how auto callables work and how these ETFs are structured. We'll certainly get into why investors are looking at solutions like these and where they fit in a portfolio and then going back to cover call ETFs.
turns.zh: 所以 Simeon Hyman 要带我们讲清楚自动赎回型是怎么运作的、这些 ETF 又是怎么搭建结构的。我们肯定会聊到投资者为什么在看这类方案、它们在组合里如何定位，然后回到备兑看涨 ETF。

turns.en: ProShares actually has a suite of those as well, an ETF like the ProShares NASDAQ 100 High Income ETF. So we'll also touch on that lineup as part of our conversation.
turns.zh: ProShares 其实也有一整套备兑看涨产品，比如 ProShares NASDAQ 100 High Income ETF。所以我们的对话里也会涉及这条产品线。

turns.en: Now, later, I'll be joined by one of my favorite ETF analysts, the always witty Todd Sohn, Chief ETF Strategist at Barrett Strategas. And of course, Barrett Strategas is one of the top macro research firms on Wall Street and Todd heads up all of their ETF research and coverage there.
turns.zh: 之后我还要请到我最喜欢的 ETF 分析师之一、永远妙语连珠的 Todd Sohn，Baird Strategas 的首席 ETF 策略师。Baird Strategas 当然是华尔街顶级的宏观研究机构之一，Todd 在那边主管全部的 ETF 研究和覆盖。

turns.en: And so this should be fun. We are just going to go around the world of ETFs. I have a bunch of topics for us to get into everything from sports futures contract ETFs to the record number of new launches, which that was just set last week, by the way, we'll get into Corgi ETFs.
turns.zh: 所以这期一定很有意思。我们要在全球 ETF 世界里转一圈。我准备了一大堆话题要聊，从体育期货合约 ETF 到新发行数量的破纪录——顺便说那项纪录就是上周刚刷新的，我们要聊 Corgi ETF。

turns.en: I'm sure I'll try to work in some crypto ETFs as well. If nothing else, I promise you'll be entertained as Todd and I try to make sense of the current state of ETFs.
turns.zh: 我肯定也会尽量塞进一些加密货币（crypto）ETF。再不济，我保证你们会被逗乐，因为我和 Todd 要试着把当前 ETF 的状态理出个头绪。

turns.en: As always, questions or comments, you can find me on X at Nate Jiracy, or you can go to ETFprime.com. So first up this week is ProShares, Simeon Hyman, who is joining me from New Jersey.
turns.zh: 照例，有任何问题或评论，可以在 X 上找我，Nate Geraci，或者直接去 ETFprime.com。所以本周第一个登场的是 ProShares 的 Simeon Hyman，他正从新泽西跟我连线。

turns.en: Simeon, it is always great having you on here. Welcome back to the podcast. Thanks so much for having me. All right. So back in August, ProShares launched these three auto-callable ETFs.
turns.zh: Simeon，有你来做客永远太好了，欢迎回到节目。非常感谢邀请我。好，八月 ProShares 推出了这三只自动赎回型 ETF。

turns.en: There's one on the S&P 500, ticker ACSP, one on the NASDAQ 100, ticker ACQQ, and then one on the Russell 2000, ticker ACRT. To start, I think you know, I always like covering the basics.
turns.zh: 一只是挂钩标普 500（S&P 500）的，代码 ACSP；一只是挂钩纳斯达克 100（NASDAQ 100）的，代码 ACQQ；还有一只是挂钩罗素 2000（Russell 2000）的，代码 ACRT。先从开头说起，我一直喜欢先把基础讲清楚。

turns.en: And my sense is when some investors hear the term auto-callable, that sounds pretty complex, maybe even a little bit intimidating. So do you first want to explain what an auto-callable is and how it works at a high level and then we can certainly talk about the ETFs?
turns.zh: 我的感觉是，有些投资者一听到"自动赎回型"这个词，听着挺复杂，甚至有点吓人。所以你能不能先大致解释一下什么是自动赎回型、它怎么运作，然后我们再具体聊这些 ETF？

turns.en: Sure. So as you noted, the most important thing is to start with the basics. And auto-callables have been around for a while. They have been around traditionally sourced through a structured note.
turns.zh: 好。正如你说的，最重要的还是从基础讲起。自动赎回型已经存在有一段时间了，传统上它是通过结构化票据（structured note）来发行的。

turns.en: And the way that note works is, as you were indicating, alternative income, where sometimes folks refer to the category as derivative income.
turns.zh: 那种票据的运作方式，就像你提到的，另类收益，有时人们把这个类别叫作衍生收益（derivative income）。

turns.en: I also like to think of it as income generated from equity risk. And that's how an auto-callable works. You get a level of income, a coupon, you get your money at maturity, unless the underlying equity index drops below a certain level.
turns.zh: 我也喜欢把它理解成来自股票风险的收益。自动赎回型就是这么运作的。你获得一档收益、一笔票息（coupon），到期时拿回本金，除非标的股票指数跌破某个水平。

turns.en: That is the classic payoff profile of an auto-callable. And that level of income can be quite generous in the mid to high teens sometimes. And again, you will get that principle back unless the equity market or the equity index that's driving your specific auto-callable drops below a significant level.
turns.zh: 这就是自动赎回型经典的收益形态。而这档收益可以相当慷慨，有时在 15% 到中高位之间。并且再强调一下，除非驱动你这笔自动赎回型的股票市场或股票指数跌破一个显著水平，你会拿回本金。

turns.en: And that's been very attractive, but it's been limited because the way to access it has been through these structured notes. And when you do it in a structured note, you kind of can't just own one because it matters the day you enter, because that establishes where the downside risk is, establish the coupon, all these things.
turns.zh: 这一直很有吸引力，但受限，因为接触它的途径是这些结构化票据。而当你用结构化票据来做时，你没法只持有一只，因为你入场的日子很重要，它决定了下行风险在哪里、票息是多少，凡此种种。

turns.en: So in order to manage a strategy, effectively, you needed to have a diversified portfolio of these. And that tells you a lot about why they were popular because they're an excellent source of equity income, income not related to interest rate risk.
turns.zh: 所以为了有效地管理一个策略，你需要持有一篮子分散化的这类票据。这一点其实很好地解释了它们为什么受欢迎，因为它们是绝佳的股票型收益来源，与利率风险无关的收益。

turns.en: But it also tells you a little bit about why they haven't quite blossomed across the full landscape because of the challenges of accessing them through those individual structured notes.
turns.zh: 但同时也说明了为什么它们在整个市场里还没有完全爆发，因为通过单只结构化票据去接触有种种障碍。

turns.en: Yeah, and maybe talk a little bit more about your last point there, because I mentioned at the top, this is a rapidly expanding ETF category in auto-callable ETFs.
turns.zh: 是啊，能不能再展开讲讲你最后那一点，因为我开头提到过，自动赎回型 ETF 是一个快速扩张的 ETF 类别。

turns.en: You mentioned the more generous income here, a little bit of a different maybe risk return profile compared to some other traditional investments.
turns.zh: 你这里提到收益更慷慨，与一些其他传统投资相比，也许是不同的风险回报特征。

turns.en: Is that really what's driving this investor interest, along with the fact that we now have this supply coming online? Or are there any other factors you would point to?
turns.zh: 真正驱动这种投资者兴趣的是这个吗，加上我们现在看到供给开始上线？还是你会指出其他因素？

turns.en: From the environment standpoint, the demand is coming from the need for income. On the front end of Gen X, we don't have defined benefit plans.
turns.zh: 从环境层面看，需求来自于对收入的需要。在 X 世代前端这一代，我们没有固定收益养老金计划。

turns.en: And the boomers right before me don't have defined benefit plans. And if you do the math, 60-40 portfolio, even with a generous five or six percent yield on your fixed income, that's two, two and a half percent.
turns.zh: 我前面那批婴儿潮一代也没有固定收益养老金计划。你要是算一笔账，60/40 组合，就算你的固定收益部分给到 5% 到 6% 的慷慨收益率，那也就 2%、2.5%。

turns.en: That's not enough for people to run their lives on. And so you need more income. But also in this environment, as we know, it's yield up priced down.
turns.zh: 这不足以让人们靠它过日子。所以你需要更多收益。而且在这个环境里，我们都知道，收益率上行、价格下行。

turns.en: So fixed income in and of itself has a level of risk we haven't seen. In quite some time. So the need for more income and the need for income that's not related to interest rate risk, those are the environmental drivers.
turns.zh: 所以固定收益本身就带有了我们很久没见过的风险。需要更多收益，以及需要与利率风险无关的收益，这两点是环境上的驱动因素。

turns.en: And that's why this derivative income category or alternative income category has blossomed so much. Now, the category is over $200 billion.
turns.zh: 这也是为什么这个衍生收益或另类收益类别增长得这么快。现在整个类别超过 2000 亿美元。

turns.en: Now, most of that is in covered calls. And we'll touch a little bit about that at the end. We're actually at the front end of the autocollable growth.
turns.zh: 其中大部分在备兑看涨里。我们最后也会聊一点那个。在自动赎回型的增长上我们还处在前端。

turns.en: We're only up to five or six billion dollars in autocollables, that there's a real opportunity here. And the reason that the ETFs are taking off is that they solve for the challenge of the autocollable process, which is two-fold one, the diversification aspect, the need for more than for multiples of them.
turns.zh: 自动赎回型才到五六十亿美元，这里是真的有机会。而 ETF 之所以起飞，是因为它们解决了自动赎回型流程中的难题，这个难题是两方面的：一是分散化，你需要持有多只。

turns.en: And then, of course, the ability to just get them in a simple ETF wrapper. And that's the solution that we brought to market with our three ETFs.
turns.zh: 然后当然就是能够用一个简单的 ETF 外壳去持有。这就是我们带着这三只 ETF 推向市场的解决方案。

turns.en: AC triple Q on the NASDAQ 100, ACSP on the S&P 500 and ACRT on the Russell 2000. What you get with our ETFs is that ladder packaged in an ETF, diversified one-stop shopping, and we can talk more about the details.
turns.zh: 纳斯达克 100 上的 ACQQ、标普 500 上的 ACSP、罗素 2000 上的 ACRT。你从我们的 ETF 里得到的是一架梯级组合（ladder）被打包进了 ETF，一站式分散化，细节我们可以再聊。

turns.en: But that's why the ETF delivery of autocollables is taking off. Well, yeah, let's actually get into those details and help people better understand what's going on underneath the hood here.
turns.zh: 但这正是 ETF 形式的自动赎回型在起飞的原因。对，那我们不如深入到这些细节里，帮大家更好地理解引擎盖底下到底发生了什么。

turns.en: So if we take maybe ACSP, the ProShares S&P 500, autocollable income ETF, just walk through what's actually going on here. If somebody looks through into the ETF.
turns.zh: 那我们拿 ACSP、也就是 ProShares S&P 500 自动赎回型收益 ETF 举例，讲讲里面到底在干什么。如果有人看透这只 ETF 内部。

turns.en: I'll take you through a quick step-by-step. So in ACSP, we start with the S&P 500 just off the shelf. Now, the first thing that we do is create, and this is all indexed by index.
turns.zh: 我给你快速一步一步过一遍。在 ACSP 里，我们先拿现成的标普 500。然后我们做的第一件事是创建一个，这全部是指数化（indexed by index）的。

turns.en: So this is not anything that we're doing at ProShares other than following the index. So I'm following the strategy here. You take the S&P 500 and you create a volatility targeted underlying index to drive the performance of the autocollable notes.
turns.zh: 所以这不是 ProShares 在做什么别的，只是跟随指数。我跟随的是这个策略。你拿标普 500，创建一个波动率目标（volatility targeted）的底层指数，来驱动自动赎回票据的表现。

turns.en: And that's very important because by targeting a constant level of volatility, that allows for the income stream from the autocollables to be quite stable.
turns.zh: 这非常重要，因为通过锁定一个恒定的波动率水平，可以让来自自动赎回型的收益流相当稳定。

turns.en: So step one, vol targeted version of the S&P 500. That drives the performance of the autocollable index. Then each of those is manifested in one synthetic autocollable.
turns.zh: 第一步，标普 500 的波动率目标版本。它驱动自动赎回型指数的表现。然后每一笔被体现为一个合成的自动赎回型。

turns.en: We execute these through SWAP. Now here's the key. In the ETF, the autocollable issued every single week. They cannot be called for a year. They have a three year maturity.
turns.zh: 我们通过互换（swap）来执行这些。现在是关键。在 ETF 里，自动赎回型每一周发行一笔，一年内不能被赎回，期限是三年。

turns.en: If you do the math in your head, that means they're at least 52 and up to 156 of these individual notes that are now a fully diversified autocollable ladder in the ETF and that results in the index and then the ETF ACSP in this example.
turns.zh: 你要是心算一下，这意味着至少有 52 只、最多 156 只这样的单独票据，构成 ETF 里一个完全分散化的自动赎回型梯级组合，然后形成指数，再在本例里形成 ETF，即 ACSP。

turns.en: I was actually poking around on the ProShares website this morning and I saw there's a dashboard on each of these ETFs where investors can see the details of the autocollable ladder that you were just alluding to.
turns.zh: 今天早上我还在 ProShares 官网上逛了逛，我看到每只 ETF 都有一个仪表板（dashboard），投资者在里面可以看到你刚才提到的那个自动赎回型梯级组合的细节。

turns.en: Do you want to expand on that? That's obviously a nice tool for investors to be aware of. We wanted everybody to be able to have full transparency.
turns.zh: 你能展开说说吗？那显然是个值得投资者了解的好工具。我们想让每个人都能有完全的透明度。

turns.en: So when you go to our website, each of these autocollable notes are on a dashboard. They got a dot for each single one. You can see where they are.
turns.zh: 所以你到我们的网站，每一只自动赎回型票据都在仪表板上。每一笔都有一个点。你可以看到它们在哪里。

turns.en: You can see where they're priced because there's transparency now. These are all out there every single day in the old structured note world, a little more opaque.
turns.zh: 你可以看到它们的定价，因为现在有了透明度。这些每天都摆在外面，而在过去结构化票据的世界里，就更不透明一些。

turns.en: And you can see things as an example, what the yield is currently on that diversified portfolio of autocollable notes. Today, it's in the high teens.
turns.zh: 你还能举个例子看到，这一篮子分散化的自动赎回型票据当前收益率是多少。今天在 15% 以上的高位。

turns.en: You can see how many are out there. There have been 70, 80, 90, depending on our ETFs, so lots of diversification. And you can also see how close they are to either being called or their maturity.
turns.zh: 你可以看到有多少只在外面。根据我们的 ETF，有 70、80、90 只，所以高度分散化。你还能看到它们离被赎回或到期有多近。

turns.en: So you get all the information for all of the autocollables that are in the ETF at any given point. So let me ask you this because I think the question that a lot of people have is, okay, I get that there's higher income here.
turns.zh: 所以在任一时点，你都能得到 ETF 里所有自动赎回型的完整信息。那我想问你，因为我觉得很多人心里的问题是：好，我明白这里收益更高。

turns.en: I understand how autocollables work, but where exactly do these fit in a portfolio? And I'm curious how you think about the risk reward profile of an ETF, like we just walked through where you do typically have higher income than traditional bonds and other income producing investments.
turns.zh: 我理解自动赎回型怎么运作，但这些到底在组合里怎么定位？我也很好奇你怎么看我们刚才过的那种 ETF 的风险回报特征——它通常比传统债券和其他产生收益的投资收益更高。

turns.en: But there is that downside risk, right? In the event of a significant market drawdown. So again, I'm just trying to think of portfolio application.
turns.zh: 但存在那个下行风险，对吧，在市场出现大幅回撤的情况下。所以我就是想弄明白组合里的应用。

turns.en: Does this fit in the equity sleeve of a portfolio, the fixed income sleeve? How do you think investors should view these? If you go back to the payoff profile I described, we can translate that into the classic four quadrants of things that might happen in the world.
turns.zh: 它到底该放在一个组合的股票部分，还是固定收益部分？你觉得投资者应该怎么看待这些？如果你回到我描述的那个收益形态，我们可以把它翻译成世界上可能发生的经典四象限。

turns.en: So if the markets are going up, boom, you're just going to get the income. Simple enough. Now, if markets are flat, you're still going to get that income because nothing bad happened.
turns.zh: 如果市场向上，好，你就只管拿收益，简单明了。市场持平，你照样拿到那笔收益，因为什么都没变坏。

turns.en: If the markets are down just a little bit, you're still going to get the income and you're going to get your principal. But the risk is in that third quadrant, which is absolutely important for you to note, Nate, that in a significant market drawdown, you can have principal loss.
turns.zh: 市场稍微跌一点，你照样拿到收益，也拿回本金。但风险在第三个象限，这一点绝对重要，Nate 你得注意，在市场大幅回撤时，本金是会亏损的。

turns.en: So you are taking equity risk. Now, if you think about where this belongs in a portfolio, you can think of it as two ways. One, if you want to put it in the alternative bucket, back in my old, old days, we used to make the kind of simple definition of two kinds of alternatives.
turns.zh: 所以你在承担股票风险。你要是想它在组合里归到哪，可以从两个角度看。一是你想把它放进另类（alternative）这个桶。在我很早很早的年代，我们习惯把另类简单分成两类。

turns.en: Fixed income alternatives and equity alternatives. This guy is based off equity risk. So if it's in your alts bucket, it's an equity alternative.
turns.zh: 固定收益类另类，和股票类另类。这家伙是基于股票风险的。所以如果它在你另类桶里，那它就是股票类另类。

turns.en: With that diversified basket, you do over the course of time have something that looks pretty much like equity risk. So you could put it in your core equity portfolio too, to be generating equity income from that equity allocation.
turns.zh: 有了这一篮子分散化组合，随着时间推移它看起来 pretty much 就像股票风险。所以你也可以把它放进你的核心股票组合，从那部分股票配置里产生股票收益。

turns.en: So either of those is an appropriate placement in a portfolio. Okay, but just to be clear, the best market environment for an auto callable ETF is probably one in which stocks are sort of trending sideways or maybe even down somewhat, right?
turns.zh: 所以这两种放法在组合里都是合适的。好，但说清楚一点，自动赎回型 ETF 最好的市场环境，大概是股票横盘整理、甚至略微下跌的那种，对吧？

turns.en: Obviously not a massive drawdown, but essentially a sideways choppy market or even a generally negative environment. That's typically best for these, correct?
turns.zh: 显然不是大幅回撤，但基本上是横盘震荡的市场，或者甚至是普遍偏负面的环境，这类通常对这些产品最有利，对吧？

turns.en: See, I think that's absolutely a fine use case and that's a great way to get equity income in a sideways market, but in an upward trending market as well, to be able to get mid to high teens income is also quite attractive.
turns.zh: 我觉得这完全是一个不错的用例，也是在横盘市场里获取股票收益的好办法，但在向上趋势的市场里同样能拿到 15% 到高位区间的收益，也极具吸引力。

turns.en: So I would add that to a environment that's pretty well managed for auto callables as well. Will the income come down if stocks are racing ahead because the notes keep getting called and so maybe the income isn't quite as high?
turns.zh: 所以我会把上行环境也算进自动赎回型能很好管理的范围里。如果股票一路狂奔，收益会降下来吗，因为票据不断被赎回，也许收益就不那么高了？

turns.en: Still high relative to other income producing investments, but maybe not as high as if you were in that choppy sideways environment. So that's the really nice thing about the diversified ladder because not only does it diversify risk, you remember, even if you just have 70 or 80 or 90 of these things, like that's a lot of diversification, but it also smooths the income.
turns.zh: 相比其他产生收益的投资仍然算高的，但也许不如你处在那个横盘震荡环境里那么高。这正是分散化梯级组合真正妙的地方，因为它不只分散风险——你想想，哪怕你只有 70、80、90 只，那也已经是很大的分散化了——它还平滑了收益。

turns.en: So the income is smoother than you would think. You would think that there would be some volatility in income, but there are two elements here that keep the income smooth.
turns.zh: 所以收益比你想象的更平滑。你可能以为收益会有一些波动，但这里有两个要素让收益保持稳定。

turns.en: Remember, we started with the volatility targeted underline. So that guy is actually levering up and down the equity markets. If equity markets are placid, levels it up a little bit.
turns.zh: 记住，我们从一个波动率目标的底层资产开始。那家伙实际上在给股票市场加杠杆和减杠杆。如果市场平静，它就稍微加一点杠杆。

turns.en: If they're volatile, it actually delevers them. So that in and of itself smooths the income. And then the fact that you're issuing these every single week and if one's called, there's one right behind it.
turns.zh: 如果市场波动大，它实际上会去杠杆。所以这一点本身就平滑了收益。再加上你每周都在发行新的一笔，如果一笔被赎回，后面紧跟着又有一笔。

turns.en: So the income from our approach at ProShares is actually reasonably smooth. And, you know, I'd be remiss if I didn't note that there's also the opportunity for tax advantage here.
turns.zh: 所以 ProShares 这套方法带来的收益其实是相当平滑的。而且，我要是不指出这里还有税务优势的机会，那就不尽职了。

turns.en: So a decent portion of these distributions can be return of capital. And I know there are a couple of different meanings of return of capital.
turns.zh: 所以相当一部分分配可以是资本返还（return of capital）。我知道资本返还有一两种不同的含义。

turns.en: So I'll be super specific. 1099 box three non-tiven and income reduction of basis and deferral of tax. All right. And then before we move on, because I do want to ask you about covered call ETS, just going back to thinking about the downside risks.
turns.zh: 所以我说得特别具体：1099 表格第三栏，非已实现所得，降低税基，递延纳税。好，在我们往下走之前，因为我确实想问问你备兑看涨 ETF，就回到那个下行风险的思考。

turns.en: So these auto callables, they have this downside barrier, which if it's breached and stays below there at the observation period, then that would be the point at which an investor may have principle at risk.
turns.zh: 这些自动赎回型有一个下行障碍线，如果跌破了并且在观察期内一直待在那条线下方，那就是投资者本金可能面临风险的时点。

turns.en: You have this diversified ladder of auto callables. Just how should investors think about that downside risk? In other words, if the market's down 30%, should they be concerned 40%, 50%?
turns.zh: 你有这一篮子分散化的自动赎回型。投资者到底该怎么看待那个下行风险？换句话说，如果市场跌 30%，他们该担心吗？跌 40%、50% 呢？

turns.en: Does it depend because you have this diversified basket? I'm just trying to add some additional context around that because the income side makes sense.
turns.zh: 会不会因为你有一篮子分散化的组合而有所不同？我就是想给那块再补充一点背景，因为收益那一侧说得通。

turns.en: People understand we're going to get a higher level of income here. But again, there's no free lunch in the markets, obviously. And so you do have that downside risk in the, in the event of a real significant drawdown, just add a little bit more color to that piece.
turns.zh: 人们明白这里能拿到更高的收益。但市场里显然没有免费的午餐，所以在真正大幅回撤的情况下你确实承担那个下行风险，就这块再多给点细节。

turns.en: When you're in one auto callable note, old school, if you literally bought one, you would have discontinuity in your payoff profile. But once you have this well diversified portfolio, the behavior in aggregate over time, the risk level looks much more like the equity, the, the equity index off the shelf.
turns.zh: 当你持有一只单体的自动赎回型票据，老派那种，如果你真的只买一只，你的收益形态会出现不连续。但一旦你有了这一篮子分散化的组合，整体随时间的表现、风险水平，看起来就更接近现成的那个股票指数。

turns.en: So you're in the zip code of S&P 500 or NASDAQ 100 or Russell 2000 risk. Once you have the diversified portfolio. And it's one of the reasons why we're, you know, really happy to have all three in the suite, because if you have a point of view, it's really the, the risk of that underlying is meaningfully represented in each of these three ETFs.
turns.zh: 所以一旦你有了分散化组合，你就是在标普 500 或纳斯达克 100 或罗素 2000 的风险"邮编范围"里。这也是为什么我们真的很高兴整个系列里三只都有，因为如果你有观点，那就是每个底层的风险在这些三只 ETF 里都得到了有意义的体现。

turns.en: Well, great overview on auto callables. And I'll just say again, I would encourage people to go to the brochures website and look at the dashboard on these ETFs, because I think it's helpful just to see how these are structured.
turns.zh: 很好，关于自动赎回型做了精彩的概述。我再强调一遍，我会鼓励大家去 ProShares 官网看看这些 ETF 的仪表板，因为我觉得亲眼看看它们怎么搭建结构很有帮助。

turns.en: You can understand the payoff profile. You can understand that downside risk. So it's just a really good visual. I'm a visual learner. And so that helped me in understanding how these products are structured.
turns.zh: 你能理解那个收益形态，你能理解那个下行风险。所以它真的是一个很好的视觉化呈现。我是个视觉型学习者，那对我理解这些产品怎么搭建结构很有帮助。

turns.en: Okay. Well, let's talk covered call ETFs. I mentioned this at the top. This is another category that we know has been rapidly expanding in the ETF universe for, for several years now.
turns.zh: 好，我们来聊聊备兑看涨 ETF。我开头就提过，这是 ETF 版图上又一个已经快速扩张了好几天的品类。

turns.en: And ProShares does have a suite of these covered call ETFs. So for example, the ProShares S&P 500 high income ETF ticker, iSPY, that has well over a billion dollars in assets.
turns.zh: ProShares 也有一整套这些备兑看涨 ETF。比如，ProShares S&P 500 High Income ETF，代码 ISPY，资产已经超过 10 亿美元。

turns.en: There are also NASDAQ 100 and Russell 2000 versions. Talk about this lineup and maybe how it's different from some other cover call strategies on the market.
turns.zh: 还有纳斯达克 100 和罗素 2000 的版本。讲讲这条产品线，也许也讲讲它跟市面上一些其他备兑看涨策略有什么不同。

turns.en: Sure. And, you know, I triple Q is our, our covered call strategy on the NASDAQ 100. And we did bring an innovation to market several years ago.
turns.zh: 好。你知道，IQQQ 是我们在纳斯达克 100 上的备兑看涨策略。我们几年前确实往市场带来了一项创新。

turns.en: You know, when you look at traditional covered call strategies, so covered call is one of the most straightforward derivative income approaches.
turns.zh: 你看传统的备兑看涨策略，备兑看涨是最直接的衍生收益方法之一。

turns.en: You sell away the upside to the equities that you own in exchange for the premium. That makes income. And that's traditionally been done on a monthly basis.
turns.zh: 你把手里持有的股票那部分上行卖出去，换取权利金，那就形成了收益。这传统上都是按月来做的。

turns.en: The challenge with doing on a monthly basis is number one. If the market goes up in the beginning of the month, then you're out. So you're sacrificing a ton of upside.
turns.zh: 按月做的难点，第一，如果月初市场就上涨，那你就出局了，所以你牺牲了大把的上行。

turns.en: And then there's this illusion of downside protection because maybe you're making even upwards of 1% of income that month. But the equity indices, if something goes wrong, they don't go down 1% a month for 10 months, they go down 10%.
turns.zh: 然后就有一种下行保护的幻觉，因为也许你某个月能赚上 1% 以上的收益。但股票指数，如果出了事，它们不会一个月跌 1% 连跌十个月，它们会跌 10%。

turns.en: And then you're down nine if you have a traditional covered call strategy, but then you can't participate in the rebound because you sold away next month's upside.
turns.zh: 于是传统的备兑看涨策略里你就跌了 9 个点，然后你又没法参与反弹，因为你把下个月的上行卖掉了。

turns.en: And so traditional covered call strategies had this kind of bad asymmetry. If you will, you get 50, 60% of the upside and you get 80 or 90% of the downside.
turns.zh: 所以传统的备兑看涨策略有这种糟糕的不对称，你要是愿意这么说的话，你只能拿到 50%、60% 的上行，却要承担 80%、90% 的下行。

turns.en: What we saw is that opportunity to fix this several years ago because daily options became available on the major indices in the US. And so we developed this suite, again, index based.
turns.zh: 我们看到的，是几年前修复这个问题的机会，因为美国的各大指数上出现了每日期权（daily options）。于是我们开发了这个系列，同样基于指数。

turns.en: So none of us are guessing anything at the end of the day, but it's an index based strategy that writes the calls on a daily basis, executes that strategy on a daily basis.
turns.zh: 所以到收盘时我们谁都不用去猜，但这是一个基于指数的策略，每日去卖出看涨期权、每日去执行这个策略。

turns.en: And when you do that, you're up to bat every single day. If you're called away, you're still up to bat the next day. So you capture the upside.
turns.zh: 当你这么做，你每天都能上场。如果你被赎回了，第二天你照样上场。所以你能抓住上行。

turns.en: In addition, the strategy actually volatility adjusts the strike price. So when markets are particularly volatile, it actually writes further out of the money, like after liberation day, that was a big saving grace for preserving the rebound that came right after liberation day last year.
turns.zh: 此外，这个策略实际上会按波动率调整行权价。所以当市场特别波动时，它其实会卖得更价外一些，比如"解放日"（Liberation Day）之后，那正是保住紧随去年解放日之后反弹的一大救命恩人。

turns.en: And when you put that all on a blender, what we've delivered in our covered call suite is the opportunity to get those attractive covered call income streams, but also really participate pretty darn closely to the full performance of equity markets.
turns.zh: 当你把这些全部搅拌在一起，我们在备兑看涨系列里带来的，是既拿到那些诱人的备兑看涨收益流，又几乎相当贴近股票市场完整表现的机会。

turns.en: And we're really excited to bring that to market. And Node I-QQ is as the NASDAQ flavor there, which of course has had lots of energy behind it, given the NASDAQ performance.
turns.zh: 我们非常高兴把它推向市场。而 NUSD-QQQ 是那里纳斯达克的风味，考虑到纳斯达克的表现，它背后自然有很多热度。

turns.en: And I guess that's the last piece I'll close on with regards to the suite. Because each of these actually behaves like it's underlying, the fact that we have a suite and the fact that we have I-QQ is meaningful.
turns.zh: 关于这个系列我就收尾讲最后一块。因为每一只实际上都像它的底层那样表现，我们拥有一整个系列、拥有 QQQ 那一只是有意义的。

turns.en: In the monthly covered call space, it almost doesn't matter what you're writing on because you're not getting that performance. And it might as well be Malaysian equities or Brazilian equities or Indonesian equities.
turns.zh: 在按月备兑看涨的世界里，你卖在什么上面几乎不重要，因为你拿不到那个表现。卖在马来西亚股票、巴西股票或印尼股票上都一样。

turns.en: But here, once you go daily, you're really getting the performance of the underlying. So when you use I-QQ for equity income, for derivative income, you're really getting NASDAQ 100 exposure.
turns.zh: 但在这里，一旦你改成每日，你真正拿到的是底层资产的表现。所以当你用 QQQ 做股票收益、做衍生收益，你真正拿到的是纳斯达克 100 的敞口。

turns.en: So let me ask you this, given the fact that you are getting that NASDAQ exposure. And this is a similar question to the one I asked you on auto-callable ETFs.
turns.zh: 那我想问你，考虑到你确实拿到了那个纳斯达克敞口。这跟我在自动赎回型 ETF 上问你的问题是类似的。

turns.en: I've just seen a lot of debate around where covered call ETFs in general fit in a portfolio. And you'll have some people say they don't necessarily fit in the fixed income sleeve because you do have real downside equity risk here.
turns.zh: 我一直看到很多关于备兑看涨 ETF 到底在组合里怎么定位的争论。会有人说它们不一定适合放在固定收益部分，因为这里你确实承担着真正的下行股票风险。

turns.en: On the other hand, since you're capping the upside in some of these products or a lot of these products, maybe they don't fit in the equity sleeve.
turns.zh: 另一方面，既然你在这些产品里、很多这类产品里给上行加了封顶，也许它们又不适合放在股票部分。

turns.en: So just talking about that, how do you view that? And again, where these might fit in a portfolio? There's no debate about this one. This is equity.
turns.zh: 所以聊聊这个，你怎么看？还是那个问题，它们在组合里可能怎么定位？这个没什么好争的，它就是股票。

turns.en: It's equity income, but it's equity risk. And that is by design, again, going to a daily basis delivers the performance profile of the underlying equity index.
turns.zh: 它是股票收益，但它是股票风险。这是有意为之，再说一遍，采用每日的方式 delivers 底层股票指数的表现特征。

turns.en: And we think that makes a lot of sense because sometimes you have a Swiss Army knife and it has kind of a stinky knife and a stinky screwdriver.
turns.zh: 我们觉得这很有意义，因为有时候你有一把瑞士军刀，上面有一把不太好的刀和一个不太好的螺丝刀。

turns.en: But here you want a real knife and a real screwdriver. You're going to get true equity performance from I-QQ. And then to the extent that you have a view of mitigating risk, you've got the risk of your asset allocation, whether it's bonds, because maybe we'll go from five to five and a half percent of the 10 year, but if there's a recession, you'll be glad you had some.
turns.zh: 但这里你要的是真正的刀和真正的螺丝刀。你从 QQQ 里会拿到真正的股票表现。然后如果你想在缓释风险上有个观点，你还有你的资产配置里的风险，比如债券，因为也许 10 年期收益率会从 5% 到 5.5%，但如果有衰退，你会庆幸手里有些。

turns.en: And so that diversification element is there or from more specifically designed elements of your alternative exposure that really do shape returns differently than equity like autocollables.
turns.zh: 所以那种分散化的要素是存在的，或者来自你另类敞口里那些被更专门设计的部分，它们真正以不同于股票的方式塑造回报，就像自动赎回型。

turns.en: But here with our daily covered call approach in I-QQ, you're not shaping returns. You're getting healthy equity income, but you're preserving, importantly, the equity returns.
turns.zh: 但在这里，用我们 QQQ 里每日备兑看涨的做法，你并没有去扭曲回报。你在拿到健康的股票收益，同时重要的是，保住了股票回报。

turns.en: Well, Simeon, excellent insight as always this week. I find both of these categories fascinating. They just continue to expand, especially the autocollables, all the interests we're now seeing there in the product coming online.
turns.zh: Simeon，本周又是精彩的洞察。我觉得这两个类别都引人入胜。它们还在不断扩张，尤其是自动赎回型，我们现在看到那里有那么多兴趣、产品也在上线。
