turns.zh: 它本质上就是我们研究、我们卖方研究的可投资结论，对吧？我们试图把钱说到做到。

turns.en: Well, I love this. And just to give people an idea in your report today, you had a bunch of great charts, but there was one that I feel like you include fairly regularly, which shows the assets and leverage long ETFs relative to inverse ETFs.
turns.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。就给大家一个概念，你今天那份报告里有一堆很棒的图表，但其中一张我觉得你相当定期地放，就是显示杠杆多头（long）ETF 相对反向（inverse）ETF 的资产和杠杆那张。

turns.en: And right now, I think that ratio is, I believe, 10 to 1, right? So $10 going into leverage long ETFs for every dollar going into inverse ETFs.
turns.zh: 现在，我觉得那个比例，我记得是 10 比 1，对吧？也就是每一美元流向反向 ETF，就有 10 美元流向杠杆多头 ETF。

turns.en: But I'm assuming you just like this as an investor sentiment gauge, correct? Because it's pretty sensitive. Totally, totally. This is, I think, a new form of sentiment in a sense, right?
turns.zh: 但我猜你喜欢它是作为一个投资者情绪的指标，对吗？因为它相当敏感。完全，完全。这，我觉得某种意义上是一种新形式的情绪，对吧？

turns.en: Historically, we always relied on the options market, the volatility curve, investor surveys, if you're in a room with 30 people, how many are bullish or bearish, and as much as the leverage space has been around for 20 years, it wasn't until COVID that it became kind of en vogue.
turns.zh: 历史上我们一直依赖期权市场、波动率曲线、投资者调查——如果你在一个 30 人的房间里，多少人看涨或看跌——而尽管杠杆这个领域已经存在了 20 年，直到新冠时期它才变得流行起来。

turns.en: I think people really discovered the power of those tools. You don't need margin, anyone complained at institution retail. And so I look at it as an enthusiasm barometer, and it's super interesting when you take just the ratio of long assets versus inverse assets, it tells you kind of how confident people are in the market, especially because most of those assets are tied to tech, semis, NASDAQ 100, right?
turns.zh: 我觉得人们真正发现了这些工具的力量。你不需要保证金，不管是机构还是零售。所以我把这当成一个热情晴雨表，特别有意思的是，你只要拿多头资产与反向资产的比值，它就能告诉你人们对市场有多有信心，尤其是这些资产大多挂钩科技、半导体、纳斯达克 100，对吧？

turns.en: That's the bulk of the US market. And so I'm still grappling with, you mentioned 10 to one today, like, what is the right number there? What is aggressive?
turns.zh: 那是美国市场的大头。所以我到现在还在琢磨，你说今天 10 比 1，到底多少才是对的那个数字？多少算激进？

turns.en: What is washed out? And that seems to be in motion every year. For what it's worth, the last few years, every time we've had a correction, you got it down to kind of the mid single digits.
turns.zh: 多少算超卖？这似乎每年都在变动。就我了解，过去几年每次我们遇到一次回调，它降到中个位数的水平。

turns.en: That was a good capitulatory level. So maybe we're still shy there, or maybe 10 to one's the right number in a few years from now, but nonetheless, despite the pullback we saw over the summer, right, especially with the Korea unwind, you're still seem by to dip activity for levered ETS.
turns.zh: 那是个很好的投降式底部水平。所以也许我们还差一点，或者也许 10 比 1 从现在起几年后是对的数，但尽管如此，尽管我们看到过夏天的回落，尤其是韩国的解套，杠杆 ETF 上你仍然能看到逢跌买入的活动。

turns.en: So maybe that's the punchline here that the activity and the loss for tech is still certainly there. Yeah. And fairly recently, that ratio was 16 to one.
turns.zh: 所以也许这里的关键结论是，科技方向的活跃度和损失仍然确实在那儿。是的。而且不久前，那个比例还是 16 比 1。

turns.en: Let me ask you this. Could you ever see it going inverse to where you have more flows going into the inverse ETFs versus the leverage long? It's possible, but I think we have a lot worse things on our hands if that's the case.
turns.zh: 我想问你，会不会有一天你看到它转向，进入反向 ETF 的资金流比杠杆多头还多？有可能，但如果是那样，我觉得我们有更糟的事情要操心了。

turns.en: I mean, that sounds like recession to me, right? In October, 2022, the ratio did get down to one to one. Now, the space was much smaller than, but that's that's the type of environment you need for this to kind of get to the area where it's more inverse AUM, the long AUM, which is a painful way to go.
turns.zh: 我是说，那对我来说听起来像衰退，对吧？2022 年 10 月，那个比例确实降到过 1 比 1。不过那时候规模比现在小得多，但那种环境才是让反向 AUM 逼近多头 AUM 所需要的，那是种痛苦的走法。

turns.en: Not out of the realm, but we're all going to be very upset if that happens. All right, we'll get into my boatload of ETF topics. One other thing I have to ask you, just because you and I are both out on X for better or worse, I think we both have a lot of fun out there.
turns.zh: 并非不可能，但如果真发生，我们都会非常难受。好，我们要进入我那一大堆 ETF 话题了。还有另外一件事我必须问你，就因为你我都在 X 上，不论好坏，我觉得我俩在那儿玩得很开心。

turns.en: But I've got to tell you, Todd, it is unbelievable how many people steal your charts from your weekly research, right? And they'll post them out on X without any attribution, which on one hand, I think that's a huge credit to you because you do have these amazing ETF charts.
turns.zh: 但我得告诉你，Todd，偷你每周研究图表的人数多到不可思议，对吧？他们把图表直接发到 X 上，一个字的出处都不标，一方面我觉得那是对你的巨大褒奖，因为你这些 ETF 图表真的太棒了。

turns.en: On the other hand, that has to be a little frustrating. Yeah. I mean, it's flattering, right? We do our best here at Stratigus. Very Stratigus.
turns.zh: 另一方面，那肯定有点让人沮丧。嗯，我觉得挺荣幸的，对吧？我们在 Strategas 尽力做到最好。非常 Strategas。

turns.en: And admittedly, I do put out a video on Stratigus asset management, which includes some of the charts from that note, just for the public, for brand awareness.
turns.zh: 坦白讲，我的确会发一个 Strategas 资产管理的视频，里面用了那篇笔记里的一些图表，就是为了公开、为了品牌认知。

turns.en: So it's partially our own fault. But at the end of the day, we make our money off of producing research for clients and trying to inform people in the markets.
turns.zh: 所以有一部分是我们自己的锅。但说到底，我们靠为客户制作研究、试图让市场里的人知情来挣钱。

turns.en: That's why it's always a little like, well, you know, if you're going to borrow a chart, at least give attribution, because people, how do you think I feed my children?
turns.zh: 所以这总是让人有点……你如果要借一张图表，至少标个出处吧，因为各位，你们觉得我怎么养我的孩子？

turns.en: Right? It's based off of this research. So we try to make it a two-way street for folks that we like. You know, you're a great person about it.
turns.zh: 对吧？这靠的就是这份研究。所以我们试着跟我们喜欢的人把这变成双向的。你知道，你在这一点上是个很好的人。

turns.en: Some other folks have peers of ours are great about it. But, you know, if you're thinking about whether it's our charts or anyone else's charts, if you're thinking about taking it or posting without attribution, just remember, some people kind of depend on their business for that, right?
turns.zh: 我们的一些同行在这方面也很好。但你要是考虑拿我们的图表或任何别人的图表，你要是想不标出处就拿走或发出去，就记住，有些人其实是靠这个吃饭的，对吧？

turns.en: We're in the for-profit research business, as we say. But try to share as nicely as possible. A hundred percent. And also, it's just some common courtesy.
turns.zh: 我们是做营利研究的，正如我们常说的。但尽量友善地分享。百分之百。而且这也是基本礼貌。

turns.en: All right. I agree. At the end of the day, this is a business, but like, use some common courtesy. All right. And where, if people want to access this weekly research that you put out, do they need to be a client of Barrett Stratigas or how can they obtain this?
turns.zh: 完全同意。说到底这是门生意，但请讲点基本礼貌。好，那大家如果想看你出的这份每周研究，需要成为 Baird Strategas 的客户吗，或者怎么获取？

turns.en: So there's two ways. You can be a client of Barrett Stratigas, right? And please reach out. We have sales folks covering the whole globe. I'm going to Asia next week.
turns.zh: 有两个途径。你可以成为 Baird Strategas 的客户，对吧？请尽管联系我们，我们有覆盖全球的销售。我下周要去亚洲。

turns.en: I'm looking forward to that. Or, apparently, if you invest through Stratigas asset management, you can also become a client through that way, right?
turns.zh: 我很期待。或者，显然如果你通过 Strategas 资产管理投资，你也能借此成为客户，对吧？

turns.en: AUM and our ETFs or SMAs is just as good as being a research client and paying through that way or trading through our trading desk, right? We have an equity trading desk, an options trading desk.
turns.zh: 在我们 ETF 或 SMA 上的 AUM，跟作为研究客户付费或通过我们交易台交易一样有效，对吧？我们有股票交易台、期权交易台。

turns.en: So Stratigas ETFs.com is a great route for Barrett Stratigas.com. Or you can just go out on X and find Todd's charts floating around for free without attribution.
turns.zh: 所以 StrategasETFs.com 是很好的途径，还有 BairdStrategas.com。或者你就上 X 去，免费找到 Todd 那些没标出处的图表到处飘着。

turns.en: Some of them will be out there. All right. Let's get into these topics I have. And here's the deal. We're just going to start hot right out of the gate.
turns.zh: 其中一些肯定在那儿飘着。好，我们来进入我准备的话题。规则是这样：我们要一上来就火力全开。

turns.en: I want you to tell me the single wildest thing you have seen in the ETF space this year. Ooh, the single wildest thing. Single wildest. Does it have to be live?
turns.zh: 我要你告诉我，今年你在 ETF 领域看到的最离谱的一件事。哦，最离谱的一件事。最离谱。它必须是已经上线的吗？

turns.en: No, you tell me. I think it's sports ETFs, futures-based ETFs. Maybe that's not the wildest, but that's what comes to mind because we're entering some strange territory there.
turns.zh: 不，你说。我猜是体育 ETF、基于期货的 ETF。也许那不是最离谱的，但它是我脑子里第一个冒出来的，因为我们正在进入一些奇怪的 territory。

turns.en: I get it and it makes sense. The industries are actually well-built. I've read the methodologies, but not everything necessarily needs an ETF.
turns.zh: 我理解，它讲得通。这些行业其实构建得很好。我读过那些方法论，但不是所有东西都非得有一只 ETF。

turns.en: So I'm very curious to see, assuming these are greenlit, how it goes. Right. So the baseball season is about to end. If you had an ETF live trading, what happens then after the season?
turns.zh: 所以我很好奇会怎么样，假设这些获批，会怎么走。对吧，棒球赛季快结束了。如果你有 ETF 在实时交易，那赛季结束后会发生什么？

turns.en: They're just going to float around like jellyfish, I think. And if you're going to tell me that the Yankees are going to sign the best player on the Brewers, the Blueers' ETF is going to tank and the Yankees will probably get a boost, but that could be ripe for insider trading.
turns.zh: 我觉得它们就会像水母一样到处飘。你要是告诉我洋基队会签下酿酒人队最好的球员，那洋基的 ETF 会……不，酿酒人的 ETF 会暴跌，洋基大概会被提振，但那可能是内幕交易的温床。

turns.en: So I don't know, I do think it's the sports stuff because that's getting out of the realm of financial assets into democratizing sports. I think it's super interesting, but I have a lot of questions of how this is just going to go during these quiet periods.
turns.zh: 所以我不知道，我确实觉得是体育这些，因为那正从金融资产的范畴跨出去，进入把体育平民化。我觉得极其有意思，但我有很多疑问：在这些沉寂期里它到底会怎么走。

turns.en: That to me is the wildest part, especially when you start adding leverage to it also. Have you looked at the volume in these contracts on the CME?
turns.zh: 那对我来说是最离谱的部分，尤其当你还开始给它加杠杆。你看过 CME 上这些合约的成交量吗？

turns.en: There's really not a lot going on there right now. There's a meme for it, I think. I can't think of it, but it's quiet. There's definitely a meme out there, because anyone care.
turns.zh: 现在那里其实没什么动静。我觉得有个关于它的梗（meme）。我想不起来了，但它很冷清。外面肯定有个梗，因为谁在乎。

turns.en: And it's probably going to take time, just like any other ETF that's happened before, whether it's high yield bond, seal, all this stuff, right?
turns.zh: 这大概需要时间，就像以前发生过的任何其他 ETF，不管是高收益债券、还是别的这些东西，对吧？

turns.en: The first few weeks when it's exotic, maybe years do take time to build it out. So maybe they just got to wait for the infrastructure to come.
turns.zh: 最初几个星期，当它还很新奇，也许好几年，都要时间去铺开。所以也许它们就是得等基础设施到位。

turns.en: But I'm just very curious. And you're going to have multiple issuers out there about who have the same ETF, right? The Milwaukee Brewers ETF across three or four different issuers.
turns.zh: 但我就是很好奇。而且你会有多家发行人在那儿，发行同一只 ETF，对吧？密尔沃基酿酒人队 ETF，散在三四个不同的发行人那儿。

turns.en: Which one do I go to? I guess who has the best spreads, who has the best fee? Maybe the most affordable fee, right? The liquidity. So I have a lot of questions.
turns.zh: 我该找哪一只？我猜看谁有最好的价差、谁有最好的费用？也许是最实惠的费用，对吧？流动性。所以我有很多疑问。

turns.en: It's very unique. I do think it might be the wildest one, though. And I'm trying to think of a better one off the top of my head. But I think it's that.
turns.zh: 非常独特。我确实觉得它可能就是最离谱的那一个。我试着在脑子里想一个更好的，但我觉得就是它。

turns.en: If I had it, can I pick a second? Oh, go ahead, go ahead. I might say I was going to say the go for it. Well, I was going to say if. All right, all right, I'm going.
turns.zh: 如果我要选的话，我能选第二个吗？哦，你说，你说。我要说的是，GO 为它。好吧好吧，我要说了。

turns.en: You go. Perpetual future swaps, I think are interesting, too. Especially given the anthropic S1 yesterday. Now, I don't know if those are going to go away once the company IPOs.
turns.zh: 你先说。我认为永续期货互换（perpetual futures）也挺有意思。特别是考虑到昨天 Anthropic 的事。我不知道这些会不会在公司 IPO 之后就消失。

turns.en: But I mean, I'm on that thing every day now on hyper liquid, Washington, anthropic and open AI. I think it's very unique and a great way to get a lens into how privates are trading.
turns.zh: 但我是说，我现在每天都盯着那个，Hyperliquid、Washington、Anthropic 和 OpenAI。我觉得那非常独特，也是了解私营公司怎么交易的一个好窗口。

turns.en: I agree. I actually think the perpetual futures contracts are a pretty elegant way to get exposure because you do have a live trading market.
turns.zh: 我同意。我其实觉得永续期货合约是一种相当优雅地获得敞口的方式，因为你确实有一个实时交易市场。

turns.en: And obviously right now, it's indirect exposure via swaps. We have the swap counterparty going and using the perpetual futures as the underlying reference.
turns.zh: 显然现在它是通过互换的间接敞口。我们有互换对手方在运作，用永续期货作为底层参照。

turns.en: But yeah, I think that's an interesting story. The other one I was going to say is, of course, Corgi launching, you know, 200 plus ETFs. They just launched like seven more ETFs with expense ratios of two basis points.
turns.zh: 但 yeah，我觉得那是个有趣的故事。我原本要说的另一个，当然是 Corgi 的发行，200 多只 ETF。他们刚又发了七只，费率 2 个基点。

turns.en: That's a pretty wild story. But real quick, I want to, coming back to the sports futures ETFs. And I think you were alluding to this, this blurring of a line between investing and gambling.
turns.zh: 那是个相当离谱的故事。但说回来，回到体育期货 ETF。我觉得你一直在暗示这个：投资和赌博之间界限的模糊。

turns.en: I'll tell you, this is a topic I've talked about a lot this year. I've gotten some great takes from people, you know, like ETF.com's Dave Nodig and ETF actions, Mike Aikens, there have been others.
turns.zh: 我告诉你，这是今年我聊过很多次的一个话题。我从一些人那儿得到过很好的观点，比如 ETF.com 的 Dave Nadig，还有 ETF Action 的 Mike Aikens，也有别人。

turns.en: Like, where do you ultimately land on this? So yes, it's a wild story in the ETF space. But like, if we take a more serious look at what's going on here, do you have any issue with something like NHL or MLB futures ETFs existing?
turns.zh: 你最终站到哪一边？所以是的，在 ETF 领域它是个离谱的故事。但如果我们更严肃地看这里到底在发生什么，你对 NHL 或 MLB 期货 ETF 这种东西的存在有没有意见？

turns.en: I don't think so, particularly because they have a proper index methodology. They have futures. I just don't know if we need them, but I don't have a problem.
turns.zh: 我觉得没有，特别是因为它们有正经的指数方法论。它们有期货。我只是不知道我们需不需要它们，但我没有问题。

turns.en: And it's never going to be the bulk of someone's portfolio, like the majority of people's portfolio, right? That's always going to be the simple 60, 40 type stuff.
turns.zh: 而且它永远不会成为某人组合的大头、多数人组合的大头，对吧？那永远会是简单的 60/40 那样的东西。

turns.en: So if you are a Yankees fan, like I am or your royals out there and you want to say, OK, I want to, I think they're going to be good this year.
turns.zh: 所以如果你是个洋基球迷，像我一样，或者你是皇家队的，你想说，好，我觉得他们今年会很强。

turns.en: I want to put some cash to work, whether it actually makes money's one thing. But it's a way to gain exposure to the team. Although, yeah, I think it's a weird line between investing and gambling.
turns.zh: 我想投点钱进去，它到底能不能赚钱是一回事。但它是获得对某支球队敞口的一种方式。不过，是的，我觉得这是投资和赌博之间一条奇怪的线。

turns.en: Like, you have no control over it. I don't necessarily have an issue with it, though. Maybe the leverage stuff is pushing it a little too far.
turns.zh: 你对此完全没有掌控。我倒不 necessarily 有意见。也许加杠杆那部分有点过头了。

turns.en: I don't know if I need leverage on this. But ETFs are always pushing the envelope. And we've got great, way crazier stuff out there, right? 3x this and that, then tracking a sports team over the course of the season.
turns.zh: 我不知道这上面我需不需要杠杆。但 ETF 总是在突破边界。而且外面有疯狂得多的东西，对吧？3 倍这个那个，比在整个赛季里跟踪一支体育球队还要夸张。

turns.en: I just don't know if they'll collect any massive amount of AUM to be frank. Yeah, I think the counter argument to these is that the financial markets exist for capital formation and for true financial hedging.
turns.zh: 说实话，我只是不知道它们能不能吸走任何大量的 AUM。对，我觉得反对这些的论点是，金融市场存在的意义是资本形成和真正的金融对冲。

turns.en: And this is just straight up gambling. And so, is that why financial markets exist? I think that's where people have an issue. Yeah, I don't.
turns.zh: 而这纯粹就是赌博。那么，这就是金融市场存在的理由吗？我觉得人们有意见的地方就在这。我不这么认为。

turns.en: I mean, I guess the one of the reasons I heard these were existing was to hedge team performance. But if I'm a corporate sponsor and it's found out that I'm short the ETF, I don't know what the optics of that are.
turns.zh: 我是说，我想到的它们存在的理由之一，是对冲球队的表现。但如果我是个企业赞助商，结果被发现在做空这只 ETF，我不知道那画面好不好看。

turns.en: If that's a thing, that'll happen. Well, and also, I mean, you're talking like we can count on one hand, how many people that applies to, you know, maybe two hands for people who would want to hedge a sports team's performance for true financial reasons.
turns.zh: 如果那是一回事，那它就会发生。而且，我是说，你能靠一只手数得过来，这适用于多少人，也许两只手，为了真正的金融理由想对冲一支球队表现的人。

turns.en: But in any event, I agree. Wild story. I'm fascinated to see how this unfolds. Again, I'm just watching the volume in the CME contracts and we'll see if there continues to be uptake there.
turns.zh: 但无论如何，我同意。离谱的故事。我很着迷看它会怎么展开。我再强调一下，我就盯着 CME 合约的成交量，看那里的接受度会不会继续上升。

turns.en: I think we're going to need to see that before the SEC lets these come to market. If you have no volume, obviously, it's going to be difficult for these ETFs to function properly.
turns.zh: 我觉得我们需要先看到这个，SEC 才会让这些进入市场。如果你没有成交量，那这些 ETF 显然很难正常运作。

turns.en: OK. What would be? So let's put the wildest ETF story aside. What would just be your ETF story of the year thus far? And obviously, we still have a couple of months to go, so this could change.
turns.zh: 好。那会是？我们把最离谱的 ETF 故事放一边。就你而言，今年到目前为止的 ETF 年度故事会是什么？显然我们还剩几个月，所以可能会变。

turns.en: But as we sit here today, what would be the year's biggest story to you? It's got to be the continued full blown adoption of the ETF, right?
turns.zh: 但就我们坐在这儿的今天，对你来说今年最大的故事会是什么？那一定是 ETF 的持续、全面采用，对吧？

turns.en: We're at over 1,000 launches, trillion in inflows, I believe. And I think volume probably set a record, too. And my conversations are coming from every direction.
turns.zh: 我们已经超过 1000 只新发、流入逾 1 万亿美元，我记得。我觉得成交量可能也创了纪录。我的对话来自四面八方。

turns.en: It's more fast money institutions to your legacy asset managers. I just think the ETF is definitely here. Folks are now super alarmed by mutual fund outflows.
turns.zh: 从更快的钱到机构，再到你的老牌资产管理公司。我就是觉得 ETF 确实站稳了。人们现在对共同基金的外流超级紧张。

turns.en: Maybe that stems from share classes and pulse that. But it is just this full blown proliferation. And a part of that is the market has been great for equities at least.
turns.zh: 也许那源自份额类别和 pulse 那点。但它就是这种全面的大爆发。这部分是因为市场至少对股票很好。

turns.en: But I think it's just this pure record setting adoption of the ETF has to be the story, the primary story of the year. Of course, there's some plots in there, but I think very high level.
turns.zh: 但我觉得就是这种纯粹的、破纪录的 ETF 采用，一定是今年的头号故事。当然里面有一些剧情，但我觉得很高层面看。

turns.en: It is the ETF industry going full steam ahead. I think that's always a good one. I mean, I was looking this morning, you have total ETF inflows this year over 1.7 trillion. Again, we still have a couple of months to go.
turns.zh: 就是 ETF 行业全速前进。我觉得那永远是个好故事。我是说，今天早上我看了一下，今年 ETF 总流入超过 1.7 万亿。我们仍然还有几个月。

turns.en: I was trying to think of some other big stories. We'll see what you think about this. I mean, Vanguard passing BlackRock and total ETF assets is a pretty big milestone.
turns.zh: 我试着想一些其他的大故事。我们看看你怎么想。我是说，Vanguard 在 ETF 总资产上超过 BlackRock，是个相当大的里程碑。

turns.en: They've kind of flip-flopped back and forth. But as of today, I show Vanguard is ahead of BlackRock. ETF, M&A, the mergers and acquisitions that we've seen, there's been some pretty big ones there.
turns.zh: 它们来来去去互有胜负。但就今天，我这边显示 Vanguard 领先于 BlackRock。ETF 的并购，我们看到的那些合并收购，里面有相当大的几笔。

turns.en: I think the Treasury Department, looking at so-called ETF tax avoidance strategies, is a pretty big story. We hit on the sports futures ETFs, which is a wild story, but a big one.
turns.zh: 我觉得财政部盯着所谓的 ETF 避税策略，是个相当大的故事。我们聊到了体育期货 ETF，那是个离谱的故事，但也很大。

turns.en: I think prediction market ETFs is something interesting. I don't think that's an ETF story of the year, but certainly one that's made a lot of headlines.
turns.zh: 我觉得预测市场（prediction market）ETF 是挺有意思的东西。我不认为那是 ETF 年度故事，但它确实上了很多头条。

turns.en: I don't know if anything there does anything for you. I think level two would be the M&A. A lot of shops have realized, oh, these things are valuable and they scale.
turns.zh: 我不知道那儿有没有什么对你有触动。我排名第二的会是并购。很多机构意识到，哦，这些东西有价值，而且它们能规模化。

turns.en: Especially if you have distribution. The companies that are being acquired have demand for their products. They're doing something different.
turns.zh: 尤其如果你有分销能力。被收购的那些公司，它们的产品有需求，它们在做些不一样的事。

turns.en: They're providing a solution and they have distribution. That is so important when you have, what are their 500 and some different ETF issuers out there?
turns.zh: 它们提供解决方案，而且有分销能力。当你有，它们有 500 多家不同的 ETF 发行人在外面，分销就极其重要。

turns.en: I mean, as we mentioned, 1,000 launches, standing out in the crowd. You could have a great product, but if nobody hears about it and nobody can get access to it because of a platform restriction or something like that, that's a massive headwind.
turns.zh: 我是说，正如我们提到的，1000 只新发，在人群中脱颖而出。你可能有很棒的产品，但如果没人听说、没人能接触到它——因为某个平台限制之类——那是巨大的逆风。

turns.en: I think there's going to be more M&A to piggyback off one of your predictions from way back 10 months ago. It just doesn't seem like it's over yet and may not be an established issuer.
turns.zh: 我觉得会有更多并购，也顺着你 10 个月前的一个预言往下走。它看起来远没结束，而且不一定是已成型的发行人。

turns.en: It might be one down the lead table or a company that has even started yet, right? That comes up with some unique solution out there to fit in a portfolio.
turns.zh: 也许是榜单往下的一些，或者甚至是还没起步的公司，对吧？谁能拿出某个独特的解决方案塞进组合。

turns.en: I suspect more M&A and who knows, maybe it happens at the top of the food chain too. Not that I know anything, but that's always a possibility because of how competitive this world is, especially with Vanguard being the king now.
turns.zh: 我预感会有更多并购，谁知道呢，也许顶端也会发生。不是说我有什么内幕，但那永远是个可能，因为这个世界竞争太激烈了，尤其现在 Vanguard 称王。

turns.en: Yeah, I agree with all that. I think you know, I always say distribution is king in the ETF space. I think we all agree with that. And I think M&A comes down to distribution and differentiation.
turns.zh: 是的，我完全同意。我总觉得，我一直在说，在 ETF 领域分销为王。我想我们都同意这点。我觉得并购归根结底是分销加差异化。

turns.en: If you have an ETF issuer that has differentiated products, but maybe they don't have the distribution and you have an ETF issuer that actually has the distribution to be able to get those differentiated products out to market, that's going to be a winning combination.
turns.zh: 如果你有一个 ETF 发行人有差异化的产品，但也许他们没有分销；而你有另一个 ETF 发行人确实有分销，能把这些差异化产品推向市场，那就是一个制胜组合。

turns.en: And I do think we'll continue to see more M&A. Let me ask you, again, we talk sports futures ETFs, obviously, but I mentioned prediction market ETFs.
turns.zh: 我确实觉得我们会继续看到更多并购。我想问你，我们聊体育期货 ETF 显然了，但我提到了预测市场 ETF。

turns.en: And I think you could make the case that there's a stronger investment rationale to own these, like if you're hedging political outcomes in a portfolio or something like that.
turns.zh: 我觉得你可以说持有这些有更扎实的投资理由，如果你在组合里对冲政治结果之类的。

turns.en: What do you think about prediction market ETFs? Obviously, you're pretty liberal on the sports futures ETFs. What do you think about prediction market ETFs?
turns.zh: 你怎么看预测市场 ETF？显然你在体育期货 ETF 上比较开明。那你怎么看预测市场 ETF？

turns.en: I think this Brazil thing, this election in Brazil, where both Sonaro, hopefully I'm pronouncing that was an 80% or 90% chance of winning on prediction markets and it completely missed.
turns.zh: 我觉得这次巴西这个事，巴西的这次大选，两个人——希望我发音没错——在预测市场上有 80% 或 90% 的胜算，结果完全落空。

turns.en: So in that case, I'm like, all right, maybe these are not deep enough yet. But on the other hand, I am sympathetic to the idea that, well, hey, maybe I was long Brazil equity and then short Bolsonaro.
turns.zh: 所以那种情况下我就会想，好吧，也许这些还不够深。但另一方面，我同情这个想法：嘿，也许我做多巴西股票、然后做空博索纳罗。

turns.en: That's actually makes sense to me if I'm trying to protect risk, because that would have worked out a sense, right? Maybe you made it on the prediction market, you missed on the equity or something like that.
turns.zh: 那对我其实讲得通，如果我想保护风险，因为那从某种角度是会奏效的，对吧？也许你在预测市场上赚了，在股票上亏了，或者反过来。

turns.en: People smarter than me can figure out how to structure that. So that I can understand. It makes sense for elections. I don't know if it makes sense for if Pat Mahomes is going to have three touchdowns in a game.
turns.zh: 比我聪明的人能想清楚怎么搭那个结构。所以在我看来，对选举它讲得通。我不知道对 Patrick Mahomes 一场比赛进三个达阵它讲不讲得通。

turns.en: There are economic events where I appreciate the hedging ability. It's just a matter of like, is there fraud, right? Are these protected markets, I don't know, are they deep enough and liquid enough?
turns.zh: 有一些经济事件我很欣赏它的对冲能力。问题只是，有没有欺诈，对吧？这些是不是受保护的市场，我不知道，它们够不够深、够不够流动？

turns.en: And do they actually make reasonable sense? Because I would rather not see 100 prediction markets based off of a bunch of dopey things like a Super Bowl winner or something like that, right?
turns.zh: 它们到底讲不讲得通？因为我可不想看到 100 个预测市场建立在一大堆傻乎乎的事情上，比如超级碗谁赢之类，对吧？

turns.en: I think around economic events and election events, binary outcomes make sense to me. But people, there's always going to be stories about people just blowing up their accounts like any other space.
turns.zh: 我觉得围绕经济事件和选举事件、二元结果，对我讲得通。但人们，永远会有人把自己的账户爆掉的故事，就像任何别的领域一样。

turns.en: That's the problem. So again, it goes back to the whole nascent market thing. Like these need to build out over time and also show that they're just not ripe with fraud.
turns.zh: 那就是问题。所以这又回到整个新兴市场那点。像这些需要随时间铺开，还要证明它们并非满是欺诈。

turns.en: I agree. I think that's a great take. I think it comes back to what I was saying before. I mean, the purpose of financial markets is capital formation and true financial hedging.
turns.zh: 我同意。我觉得那是个很好的观点。我觉得这回到我之前说的。我是说，金融市场的目的是资本形成和真正的金融对冲。

turns.en: And I do think there are a number of prediction markets, exactly what you hit on political outcomes, economic outcomes. Like if you want to, you know, predict where CPI is going to go or what the unemployment report looks like, I can see how you would have true hedging rationale and a portfolio to be involved in something like that.
turns.zh: 我确实觉得有不少预测市场，正好是你提到的政治结果、经济结果。如果你想预测 CPI 会怎么走，或者失业报告长什么样，我能看出你在组合里怎么会有真正的对冲理由去参与这种。

turns.en: If you start getting into Pat Mahome's touchdowns, obviously now we're back to the sports futures ETFs and we're gambling here. I also like it as someone who will look at the markets through ETFs.
turns.zh: 如果你开始聊 Patrick Mahomes 的达阵数，那显然我们又回到体育期货 ETF，这里我们是在赌博。我也喜欢它，作为一个会通过 ETF 看市场的人。

turns.en: It's information, right? Just as hyper liquid is information on anthropic and open AI. Okay. I can just get a sense of what does the market think about some upcoming event, assuming it's deep enough, right?
turns.zh: 它是信息，对吧？就像 Hyperliquid 是关于 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的信息。好。我能感觉到市场对某个即将发生的事件怎么看，前提是它够深，对吧？

turns.en: What is my, what is my end sample size on this? What is the volume on a certain contract? That will be extremely important over time. All right.
turns.zh: 我的样本量是多少？某个合约的成交量是多少？那随着时间会极其重要。好。

turns.en: While we're in this realm of prediction markets, I'm actually going to use this spot to broach the topic of crypto ETFs and some people view crypto is gambling.
turns.zh: 在我们还在预测市场这块的时候，我正好借这个机会引出加密货币 ETF 的话题，有些人觉得加密货币就是赌博。

turns.en: Obviously there's a prediction market element, depending upon the platform you're using, which by the way, do you view crypto as gambling? No, no, I think crypto has been allowed relatively long enough to fit in the portfolio and depending on which crypto, I think Dogecoin is gambling, maybe that is a little bit more gambling, but I do think crypto is slowly making its way into a reasonable allocation
turns.zh: 显然有一个预测市场的元素，取决于你用的是哪个平台，顺便说，你觉得加密货币是赌博吗？不，不，我觉得加密货币已经被允许足够长的时间、可以放进组合里了，而且取决于哪种加密货币，我觉得狗狗币（Dogecoin）是赌博，也许那更像是赌博，但我确实觉得加密货币正慢慢成为组合里一个合理的配置。

turns.en: in the portfolio. You've come a long way here, I think, from when we first started talking about this. Well, okay. So on the topic of ETFs, do you have any new views or thoughts around crypto ETFs themselves?
turns.zh: 我觉得你一路走来很远了，从我们最开始聊这个话题算起。好，那在 ETF 这个话题上，你对加密货币 ETF 本身有没有什么新的看法或想法？

turns.en: Like anything here that piques your interest in flows, launches or otherwise? I full disclosure, in my PA, I own hyper liquid, one of the ETFs, I'm not going to say which ticker, there's a couple of them out there, but I own that in my personal account, right?
turns.zh: 这里有没有什么——流、发行或者其他——引起你的兴趣？坦白说，在我个人的账户（PA）里，我持有 Hyperliquid，其中一只 ETF，我不说是哪个代码，外面有几只，但我在我的个人账户里持有它，对吧？

turns.en: Because I still don't understand a lot of crypto, like what it does, the whole infrastructure, but it's still way beyond me. But I factored that I can go on this website and show my team here, even did it this morning.
turns.zh: 因为我到现在对很多加密货币还是搞不懂，它到底干什么、整个基础设施，那仍然远远超出我的理解。但考虑到我可以上这个网站给我的团队展示，今天早上还这么做了。

turns.en: We looked at Anthropik on the chain or whatever, like that's really neat to me. It's going to be volatile. I know that for sure. But that, to me, is more disruptive and interesting and who knows where it goes.
turns.zh: 我们在链上看 Anthropic 什么的，那对我来说真新鲜。它会很波动，这个我敢肯定。但那个，对我来说更具颠覆性和有意思，天知道它会走向哪里。

turns.en: But I'm like, okay, I want a piece of that. I think the launches have calmed down if I'm not mistaken, because for a while there, we were getting real silly.
turns.zh: 但我就想，好，我要沾一点那个。我觉得发行已经慢下来了，如果我没记错的话，因为有一阵子我们真的在乱来。

turns.en: Just throwing out the two ex-dose coins, the this, the that, all sorts of different ways to spin it. And I think that coincidentally was part of this bear market we've seen.
turns.zh: 就是乱发这个那个狗狗币，这个那个，各种花样的包装。我觉得那碰巧也是我们看到的这波熊市的一部分。

turns.en: But I do like this idea, I think, the building out of active, right? I mean, to mention in ticker, like T-Row has this TKNZ. I know it's new.
turns.zh: 但我确实喜欢这个想法，我觉得，是主动化管理的建立，对吧？我提到一个代码，像 T. Rowe 有这只 TKNZ。我知道它很新。

turns.en: The assets aren't massive yet, but like, that's the future to me, right? If you don't understand the space and you're like, I want some Bitcoin, I want some Solana, Ethereum, like this active approach to moving different levers around, I think, is really enticing.
turns.zh: 资产还不算大，但我觉得，那才是未来，对吧？如果你不懂这个领域，然后你想，我要点比特币、我要点 Solana、以太坊，这种主动地拨弄不同杠杆的做法，我觉得很诱人。

turns.en: It has an important future. Yeah, I'm massively bullish on, on index-based and active crypto ETFs, even though it's still, it's been a bit slow.
turns.zh: 它有一个重要的未来。是的，我极其看好基于指数和主动管理的加密货币 ETF，尽管它到现在还是有点慢。

turns.en: Yeah, like model crypto, maybe is a word for the future. I like it. Like I said, you've come a long way here. I'm impressed. And even owning a hype and your, your PA.
turns.zh: 是的，像 model crypto，也许是未来的一个词。我喜欢。我说了，你一路走来很让人佩服，甚至在你个人账户里持有 Hyperliquid。

turns.en: All right. If we put aside some of the, the hot sauce, hot sauce stuff, the wilder stuff, right? We're talking crypto, sports, futures, ETFs, prediction markets.
turns.zh: 好，如果我们把一些辣椒、辣的东西放一边，那些更野的，对吧，我们聊的加密货币、体育、期货、ETF、预测市场。

turns.en: I'll note that there have already been nearly 1,200 new ETFs launched this year, which that's a record that was set last week. And if you look at these, you know, there are plenty of more traditional investment strategies.
turns.zh: 我要指出，今年已经发了将近 1200 只新 ETF，那是上周刚创下的纪录。你要是看这些，里面有很多是更传统的投资策略。

turns.en: It's not like all of these are hot sauce or gambling products. There are a lot of those, but it's certainly not all 1,200. And so my question for you, you, you track this closely.
turns.zh: 并不全是辣椒或赌博产品。那些确实有不少，但显然不全是那 1200 只。所以我的问题给你——你盯着这块盯得很紧。

turns.en: Again, I seen your weekly research report, you're putting new filings and you see all the stuff coming out. Where do you see white space for ETF product development?
turns.zh: 再一次，我看过你的每周研究报告，你会放上新的申报，你能看到所有出来的东西。你在哪里看到 ETF 产品开发里的空白空间？

turns.en: Like if you were an issuer, where would you be looking to launch product? Would you be going after all this hot sauce? Because that's the only area you can really differentiate or do you see white space in more traditional areas of the market?
turns.zh: 如果你是一个发行人，你会去哪里找产品来发？你会去追所有这堆辣椒？因为那是你唯一真正能差异化的领域，还是你在市场更传统的地方看到空白？

turns.en: It's a great question. It's a million dollar question. I see white space in active thematic, right? We've had this thematic flood this year.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。这是百万美元的问题。我在主动主题（active thematic）里看到空白，对吧？我们今年有这股主题洪流。

turns.en: There's over a hundred new thematic ETFs. That is a crazy amount of thematic stuff and rightfully so, right? It's a complement to a portfolio.
turns.zh: 有一百多只新主题 ETF。那是数量惊人的主题类产品，而且合情合理，对吧？它是组合的补充。

turns.en: You're trying to take advantage of the AI and semi story, the splicing and dicing of the semi space, whether it's memory, hardware, neoclabs, etc.
turns.zh: 你想利用 AI 和半导体的故事、半导体领域的精挑细选，不管是存储、硬件、新云（neocloud）等等。

turns.en: But I think it's important given how big some of these companies are and how essentially are to the infrastructure, this whole AI story to have an active manager at the wheel, right?
turns.zh: 但我觉得，考虑到有些公司有多大、对基础设施有多关键，这个 AI 大故事里让一个主动管理者掌舵很重要，对吧？

turns.en: Index thematic, they can come to the flaws. If one of those two of those companies fault there, the whole ETF is going to get messed up. So I think more active thematic, and ideally, if they're good at their job, they know the companies that are kind of on the up and coming.
turns.zh: 指数主题，它们会暴露缺陷。如果里面哪两家公司出问题，整只 ETF 就要完蛋。所以我更倾向主动主题，理想情况下，如果他们称职，他们会知道哪些公司在崛起。

turns.en: And then I do wonder active crypto. And I'm trying to figure out maybe something fixed income, you know, in duration management, like actively, there's one product that actually manages the treasury curve.
turns.zh: 然后我确实会想主动加密。我在琢磨也许固定收益里的什么，比如久期管理，主动地，有一只产品其实是在管理国债曲线。

turns.en: That might be important going forward. And I'm sure someone's going to come up with some derivative product that I'm totally unfamiliar with, not too dissimilar to buffers a few years ago, option income and now auto callable, right?
turns.zh: 那未来可能很重要。我也确信有人会搞出一个我完全不熟悉的衍生品，跟几年前 buffers、期权收益、再到现在的自动赎回型，没太大差别，对吧？

turns.en: What is the next lever of the structured node space that I frankly don't know about that is going to be the next area. But I do go back to active thematic, super important because how big that space is getting and how many products we've seen the delusion of that.
turns.zh: 结构化票据领域里下一个我不熟悉的杠杆会是什么、会成为下一个领域。但我确实回到主动主题，极其重要，因为那个空间有多大、我们已经看到那么多产品的泛滥。

turns.en: I think that's a good call. And there's been a lot more momentum in general around thematic ETFs over the past year. We had a lowl a couple of years back after that big run up in 2021.
turns.zh: 我觉得那是个好判断。过去一整年，主题 ETF 普遍有了更多动能。前几年在 2021 那波大涨之后有过一个低谷。

turns.en: And so that's definitely come back. And it sounds like just in general, you think active management, you know, whether we're talking thematics, crypto, you think fixed income, active management is what you would lean into.
turns.zh: 所以它确实回来了。听起来总体来讲，你觉得主动管理——不管我们聊主题、加密——你觉得固定收益、主动管理是你想押注的方向。

turns.en: Yeah, and maybe I'm talking our client book or just have been around our founder, Jason Schroeder loves active, right? I just think when you have 40% of the S&P is tech and everyone will say, oh, well, the other markets foreign foreign markets are more concentrated.
turns.zh: 是的，也许是我在读我们的客户簿，或者跟我们的创始人，Jason Schroeder 喜欢主动，对吧？我就是觉得，当标普 500 里 40% 是科技，人人都会说哦，其他市场、外国市场更集中。

turns.en: Yes. But how much money do you have in foreign markets? Far less than you have in the U.S. That plus where we are in this cycle, right? Moving, we're just now surpassing the fourth birthday of the bull into fear five, you now have this hyperscaler spending and credit concerns.
turns.zh: 是的。但你在国外市场里有多少钱？远少于你在美国里的。加上我们在这个周期的位置，对吧，我们才刚过牛市进入第五个年头，你现在有这些超大规模数据中心（hyperscaler）的开支和信贷担忧。

turns.en: I think it makes sense to manage risk here going forward. And so that can be active's role. Managing risk, managing concentration and surrounding the core of a portfolio that is very tech centric with active fixed income, active thematic.
turns.zh: 我觉得从这里开始管理风险讲得通。那可以是主动管理的角色。管理风险、管理集中度，用主动固定收益、主动主题去包围那个非常以科技为中心的组合核心。

turns.en: Even the derivative stuff is technically active, right? The buffers or hedged equity. That to me makes a lot of sense today than say three or four years ago when we were coming out of the bear market.
turns.zh: 甚至那些衍生品其实技术上也算主动，对吧？buffers 或对冲型股票。对我来讲，这在今天比三四年前我们刚从熊市出来时要更有意义。

turns.en: That's most important going forward right now. Other than that, I just think all the time I had the white space is just going more and more concentrated.
turns.zh: 那是现在和未来最重要的。除此之外，我一直觉得空白就是越来越集中。

turns.en: I mean, we have a new ETF that just by Samsung, TSM and Heineck's, I think, now out this week for emerging markets. Yeah. So I'm going to guess there's going to be more of that.
turns.zh: 我是说，有只新 ETF，我刚看到三星、台积电，还有喜力，我觉得，这周针对新兴市场出来了。所以我猜会有更多那种。

turns.en: Just like we're going to buy three or four ETFs that dominate an industry. There's already top 10 ones of that. I don't know if that's good white space, but it is white space.
turns.zh: 就像我们会买三四只主导一个行业的 ETF。已经有那种前十大的了。我不知道那是不是好的空白，但它是空白。

turns.en: What about Corgi who I mentioned earlier, which this is another topic. I've talked about this a bunch on here over the past couple of years.
turns.zh: 那 Corgi 呢，我前面提过，这是另一个话题。过去几年我在节目里聊过它很多次。

turns.en: I've talked about this a bunch on here over the past several months, but, you know, clearly they're not worried about where the white space is, right?
turns.zh: 过去几个月我在这儿聊过很多次，显然他们根本不担心空白在哪，对吧？

turns.en: They're like brute forcing their way into the ETF. Terror Dome. Do you think that strategy will work? Again, they're not looking for areas where there's white space in general.
turns.zh: 他们就是在硬闯 ETF 领域。整个版图。你觉得那策略会奏效吗？他们并不是在找总体上有空白的领域。

turns.en: They're just blanketing the entire market. I like it. They took a fee based approach, right? And there's still fee sensitivity. I know that's probably going away a little bit, right?
turns.zh: 他们就是在整个市场铺满。我喜欢。他们采取了以费用为基础的路子，对吧？而费用敏感度仍然存在。我知道那大概正在稍微消退，对吧？

turns.en: The fees have arguably bottomed in some segments and actually are climbing. They said, Hey, well, we can do active thematic and we're going to cut the fees in half.
turns.zh: 费用可以说在某些板块已经见底，实际上还在往上爬。他们说，嘿，我们能做主动主题，而且我们要把费用砍一半。

turns.en: Now, the tricky part is because it's active, you have to wait for that kind of seasoning period to happen, right? It's not an index that you can backtest and show people over the last 10 or 20 years.
turns.zh: 难的地方在于，因为它是主动的，你得等那种业绩沉淀期发生，对吧？它不是一个能让你回测、拿过去 10 或 20 年给别人看的指数。

turns.en: You got to let these things run for a few years before I think they finally get ground. Uh, same thing in the leverage space, cutting the fees in half.
turns.zh: 你得当它们跑上几年，我觉得它们最后才会真正落地。杠杆那块也一样，把费用砍一半。

turns.en: Same thing in the buffers. I think they did that are far lower. So I'm all about it, but going back to what we were talking about earlier. What is the distribution plan?
turns.zh: buffers 也一样。我觉得他们做的低得多。所以我完全赞成，但回到我们之前聊的。分销计划是什么？

turns.en: Right? You could have a wonderful 30 basis point theme ETF or a buffer or a levered fund, whatever your core, but if you can't get on the big platforms or pass the goal, the gatekeepers, the goalkeepers, right?
turns.zh: 对吧？你可能有一只很棒的 30 个基点的主题 ETF，或一个 buffer，或一只杠杆基金，不管你的核心是什么，但如果你上不了大平台、过不了守门人、门将，对吧？

turns.en: That's going to be really hard. So I think for them, it is the distribution and getting the why people need to buy their ETFs as opposed to just a lot of the fanfare that we all enjoy about them.
turns.zh: 那会非常难。所以我觉得对他们而言，就是分销，以及讲清楚人们为什么需要买他们的 ETF，而不是只有我们都喜欢的那种热闹。

turns.en: They seem to be getting much more aggressive on the marketing front. I feel like I'm seeing them out front facing more just in traditional financial media.
turns.zh: 他们在营销上看起来攻势大得多。我觉得我在传统财经媒体上看到他们更多地站到台前。

turns.en: I know they've gotten more active on social media. So just getting that name out there. This may sound, you know, really dumb. I agree with everything you said.
turns.zh: 我知道他们在社交媒体上也更活跃了。就是让那个名字传出去。这听起来可能真的很傻。我同意你说的每一句。

turns.en: I just wonder like, or advisors, do they want the Corgi brand on a client statement? Like, does, does even that branding, just because of the way it sounds, you think of a dog, like, do you want that on a client statement?
turns.zh: 我只是好奇，或者顾问们，他们想在客户对账单上放 Corgi 这个品牌吗？就像，单是因为它听起来像那样、你会想到一只狗，你想在对账单上放那个吗？

turns.en: I wonder if that could even be a challenge. I mean, it's a great question. I don't know how to quantify that, but I, you probably onto something there.
turns.zh: 我好奇那会不会甚至是个障碍。我的意思是，这是个好问题。我不知道怎么量化那一点，但你大概说到点子上了。

turns.en: I mean, it's the same thing as like the automobile industry, right? Do you want a foreign automobile in your driveway? Some people are very staunch about, you got to buy American or I only buy Japanese automobiles because I know the quality is pretty good.
turns.zh: 我是说，这跟汽车行业一样，对吧？你想在你家车道上放一辆外国车吗？有些人非常坚定，你必须买美国货，或者我只买日本车，因为我知道那质量很好。

turns.en: It's the same thing in ETFs, right? What is the brand that's on my statement? What do they stand for? Uh, so maybe, you know, I don't know if they need a marketing campaign of like, what do we stand for?
turns.zh: ETF 也是一样，对吧？什么品牌印在我的对账单上？它们代表什么？所以也许，我不知道他们需不需要一个像"我们代表什么"这样的营销活动。

turns.en: Right. Is it, is it lower fees for a similar product? Yeah, I, that's why I'm not in marketing, but like, what's the tag? I agree. And again, it gets back into distribution.
turns.zh: 对吧。是不是更低费用、类似的产品？是的，我之所以不做营销，但那个标签是什么？我同意。这又回到分销。

turns.en: I mean, distribution, marketing, there, there, those two are obviously tied together at the hip. Uh, but I think that'll be again, an interesting story moving forward.
turns.zh: 我是说，分销、营销，这两样显然是绑在一起的。但我觉得那又会是一个往前走的有趣故事。

turns.en: I guess on that note, we have a few, a few minutes left. Let's look ahead. Um, you give us a few ETF stories on your radar for the rest of the year and maybe into 20, 27.
turns.zh: 我想就聊到这儿，还剩几分钟。我们往前看。给我们讲几个你关注范围内的、今年余下和也许到 2027 年的 ETF 故事。

turns.en: Like what has you most interested right now is you look across the ETF landscape? Well, I'm, I'm closely waiting for this green or red light on sports.
turns.zh: 当你在整个 ETF 版图上环顾，现在最让你感兴趣的是什么？我一直在等着体育那边的绿灯或红灯。

turns.en: Right. Cause I just cause the nerd in me is, which wants to know what these things are going to do and prediction markets. Um, and I, I monitor the flows every week, just because trying to give our clients some information on what people are doing and how they're positioning.
turns.zh: 对吧，因为我骨子里那个极客想知道这些东西会干什么，还有预测市场。我每周都盯着资金流，就是想给我们的客户提供一些信息，人们在做什么、怎么布局。

turns.en: And it's, and it's been all about tech until recently, are people going to move away from tech as these concerns around spending and where we are on the cycle continue.
turns.zh: 一直到最近都是科技说了算，随着这些围绕开支的担忧、我们周期所处位置持续，人们会不会离开科技。

turns.en: Uh, and I also am trying to implore folks to look beyond the ETFs that they know of, right? We've had sector ETFs that have brown for 30 years, but there's been, there's other ETFs that are out there that can get you pretty unique sector exposure without the mega cap names weighing them down.
turns.zh: 我也一直在劝大家去看那些他们已知之外的 ETF，对吧。我们有存在了 30 年的行业 ETF，但外面还有其他 ETF，能给你相当独特的行业敞口，而不被那些大盘股压着。

turns.en: Um, and by that, I mean much more, not necessarily concentrated, but more rate sensitive or oil sensitive type ETFs. That'll be a better bet on a consumer rebound.
turns.zh: 我的意思是更……不一定更集中，而是更对利率敏感、或对油价敏感那一类的 ETF。那会是对消费反弹更好的下注。

turns.en: For example, right? You don't necessarily use a spider. That is a lot of Amazon Tesla. So I am trying to get folks to do that. Uh, and then what else?
turns.zh: 举个例子，对吧。你不一定非用一只 SPY。那里面有大量的 Amazon、Tesla。所以我在试着让大家那么做。还有什么？

turns.en: I'm very curious and I'm trying to aggregate this data on swap usage. This is fascinating to me. And I'm not talking about levered, but that is part of it too, right?
turns.zh: 我很好奇，我在试着汇总这些关于互换使用的数据。这对我很迷。我说的不只是杠杆的，但那也是其中一部分，对吧？

turns.en: The swap providers, the levered ETFs are getting more exotic. Clear street, Jane street, Ripple are going to some of the smaller house issues out there and then swap usage in plain equity ETFs unlevered.
turns.zh: 互换提供商，杠杆 ETF 变得越来越新奇。Clear Street、Jane Street、Ripple 正在去找一些更小的自管发行人，然后是普通股票 ETF 里的互换使用，无杠杆的。

turns.en: As we've talked about, you have an ETF that has three names in there. They're using swaps to get around diversification requirements necessarily.
turns.zh: 正如我们聊过的，你有一只里面只有三个成分股的 ETF。他们用互换来绕过那些分散化要求。

turns.en: Does that hit a roadblock? Probably not, but it's just very interesting that you can now build a seven stock ETF, you buy the underlying equity and then you use swaps to get around some of these, uh, diversification type requirements, I guess.
turns.zh: 这会不会撞上路障？也许不会，但只是很有意思——你现在可以搭一只七只股票的 ETF，买底层股票，然后用互换来绕过某些分散化那类要求，我想。

turns.en: And I don't know where that goes, but it's on my radar cause I keep seeing it more and more and more. Very interesting to me and who's providing it as well.
turns.zh: 我不知道那会走向哪里，但它在我雷达上，因为我一次又一次越来越多地看到它。谁在提供这些也很有意思。

turns.en: Obviously, you know, what's interesting is you went through some of those stories and then I think about what we've discussed here today. I think what I'm curious to see happen at some point, we're going to get a significant stock market drawdown.
turns.zh: 显然，你讲过那些故事之后，我想着我们今天聊的这些，我很好奇总有一天会发生、我们都会遇到一次重大的股票市场回撤。

turns.en: I'm not, you know, making a prediction here saying it's going to happen tomorrow or next month. Yeah, but at some point it's going to happen.
turns.zh: 我不是，做预测说它明天还是下个月就来。是的，但总有一天它会来。

turns.en: And I'm very curious to see, let's say we get a 30% drawdown. Does all of this stuff we're talking about here today sort of fade away? Sports, futures ETFs, um, you know, you think about all the, the swap based ETFs and some of the, you think about counterparty risks there.
turns.zh: 我非常好奇，假设我们遇到 30% 的回撤。我们今天聊的这些东西会不会都消退？体育、期货 ETF，你会想到那些基于互换的 ETF，一些，你会想到里面的对手方风险。

turns.en: I think about even some elements of crypto, you know, we can, maybe if you want to separate Bitcoin or whatever, but some elements of crypto, we talked about the new launches where you have all these leverage products coming to market.
turns.zh: 我会想到加密里的一些元素，我们可以把比特币之类分出去，但加密里的一些元素，我们聊过新发行，那里有所有这些杠杆产品涌向市场。

turns.en: We started off our discussion talking about the, uh, the ratio of leverage long ETFs to inverse ETFs where I'm heading. As I wonder what happens if we get a 30% drawdown in the equity markets?
turns.zh: 我们一开始聊的是杠杆多头 ETF 与反向 ETF 的比例，我要往哪走。我想知道，如果股票市场出现 30% 的回撤会怎样？

turns.en: Does the air sort of come out of all of that? I think that's an interesting question to think about. Absolutely. I mean, it's not too dissimilar to 22 where you had a lot of closures on the themes and leverage space.
turns.zh: 那所有这些的气会不会就泄了？我觉得那是个值得思考的有趣问题。绝对。我是说，它跟 2022 年没太大差别，那时候主题和杠杆领域有大量清盘。

turns.en: I would assume that happens too. And depending on how bad a drawdown is, right, just 20s of 30s of worse, I think this is where personally, I think legacy mutual funds who are now in the ETF space may have an advantage.
turns.zh: 我会假定那也会发生。取决于回撤有多糟，对吧，20 多的、30 多的、更糟的，我个人觉得，这就是那些现在进入 ETF 领域的老牌共同基金可能占优的地方。

turns.en: And I only say that because they have a true professional portfolio manager who can actually get on the phone with a client and try to rest like walking through what's going on.
turns.zh: 我这么说只是因为它们有一位真正的专业组合经理，能真的跟客户通上电话，试着安抚、解释正在发生什么。

turns.en: And this may be, maybe this is me pushing back on AI and, you know, robotically managed funds. Like, who are you going to call when you panic?
turns.zh: 这也许是，也许是我在反驳 AI、反驳机器人管理的基金。当你惊慌的时候，你要打给谁？

turns.en: And you want someone on the other end of that line because you need to know what is going on, what's going on in the portfolio. How are you positioning right now?
turns.zh: 你想要电话那头有个人，因为你需要知道发生了什么、组合里在发生什么、你现在怎么布局。

turns.en: I think that's going to be really important whenever the next rough waters are, um, along with a boatload of, uh, closures of a lot of the kind of the zombie ETFs that are out there.
turns.zh: 我觉得每当下一段风浪来临，那会非常非常重要， Along with 一大批那些僵尸 ETF 的清盘，外面有很多那种。

turns.en: I mean, the leverage space in general. Uh, single stock levered funds, I think like 75% of them have under 50 million assets, 25 million something.
turns.zh: 我是说，整个杠杆领域。单只股票的杠杆基金，我觉得大概 75% 的都不到 5000 万资产、2500 万之类。

turns.en: I forget the stat, but there's a lot of stuff that's going to go away. And I think that's been happening recently too. They're just, they're not, just not sticking.
turns.zh: 我记不清那个数字，但有很多东西是要消失的。我觉得最近也一直在发生。它们就是留不住。

turns.en: Yeah, I agree. I think, I don't know that I fully agree with your point on the mutual funds, but I will say clearly investors will look towards more traditional investment strategies and maybe some of this froth.
turns.zh: 是的，我同意。我想，我在共同基金那点不完全同意你的说法，但我会说，投资者显然会转向更传统的投资策略，也许我们在行业里看到的这种泡沫——

turns.en: I'll call it that we're seeing in the industry goes away, at least in the short term, I just think with the markets that we've had over the past several years, it's, it's real easy to, you know, launch products, pursue these niche areas where you may find, you know, photonics or memory, something may run, you know, really significantly, but the market's turn, that's going to change.
turns.zh: 我这么叫它——会消失，至少短期内。我只是觉得，凭过去几年我们经历的市场，推出产品、去追这些细分领域，你也许会发现光电子（photonics）或存储什么的，某个能跑得非常猛，但市场会转向，那就会变。

turns.en: That the big variable is interest rates, right? Um, the ETF industry and a lot of us haven't been around for 5% interest rates and higher if that becomes a thing.
turns.zh: 那个大变量是利率，对吧。ETF 行业，我们很多人没经历过 5% 或更高的利率，如果那成为现实。

turns.en: And that, that became, becomes real tough in terms of competition for capital for a lot of areas. Well, Todd, we will, uh, leave it there on that note.
turns.zh: 那就变得非常艰难，因为很多领域要争夺资本。好，Todd，我们就聊到这儿，就停在这个话题上。

turns.en: Always so much fun. Uh, I seriously appreciate all the work you do and covering ETFs. Uh, it's excellent. So thank you for that. Thank you for, uh, for joining me this week.
turns.zh: 总是特别开心。我真心地感谢你为覆盖 ETF 所做的全部工作，太出色了。所以谢谢你，谢谢你本周来做客。

turns.en: Thank you, Nate. You're the man. I appreciate it. That was Todd sone, chief ETF strategist at Barrage Strategas. That'll do it for this week's ETF prime.
turns.zh: 谢谢你 Nate，你是最棒的。我很感激。刚才那位是 Baird Strategas 的首席 ETF 策略师 Todd Sohn。本周的 ETF Prime 就到这里。

turns.zh: 下周我将请到 Todd Mathias，他在 Franklin Templeton 负责美国 ETF 产品策略和开发。所以我们会聊他们的红利增强（dividend boost）指数 ETF。
